texts: After a Cox-Maze IV, what most affects the need for a permanent pacemaker is doing the biatrial lesion set rather than a left-atrial-only set.
The right atrial lesions run close to the sinus node and its artery, so they cause more sinus node dysfunction, the usual reason for a pacemaker after a Maze.
Left atrial size, the duration of atrial fibrillation and adding CABG affect whether sinus rhythm returns more than whether a pacemaker is needed.
A biatrial Maze restores sinus rhythm somewhat more often, so the choice weighs rhythm control against pacing.
In the picture, the maze over both lobbies brushes the conductor's baton and the drummer marches in, while the left-only maze needs no drummer.
Memory hook: hedges in both lobbies bring the drummer.
